  `noqa` unless documented and unavoidable.
- **Types**: fix the types. No `any`, `@ts-ignore`, or `type: ignore` unless
  strictly unavoidable and explained in a comment.
- **Tests**: fix the code or the test. See "Test deletion policy" below.

### Test deletion policy

- **Tests may only be deleted when the feature they cover is removed in the
  same change.**
- If a test fails because of a code change, the code or the test must be
  updated — never simply removed.
- When in doubt, keep the test and fix the code.

## Worktrees and edit locations

Claude Code can be launched from a git worktree under
`.claude/worktrees/<name>/`. The agent's "working directory" report and the
shell cwd will point there.

**Important:** Edit / Write tool paths are absolute. If you give them a path
under `/Users/.../wevo-pulse/...` they write to the **main repo's working
tree** (on whatever branch the main repo has checked out), **not** the
worktree on its branch. Double-check the path before committing — and before
running the gate, confirm which working tree's HEAD you intend to compare
against.

When in doubt:

```bash
git -C /Users/.../wevo-pulse rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD                       # main repo branch
git -C /Users/.../wevo-pulse/.claude/worktrees/<name> rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD  # worktree branch
```

Stage and commit from the working tree you actually edited.

## Repo-specific Claude config

- `.claude/settings.json` — hooks the harness fires for `SessionStart`,
  `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`, `PreToolUse:Task`,
  `PostToolUse:Task`, and `PostToolUse:TodoWrite`. All of them shell into
  `scripts/entire-hook.sh claude-code <event>`, the same script Cursor and
  Codex use for their hook events. Do not bypass.
- `.claude/agents/entire-search.md` — `entire-search` subagent for past-work
  queries.
- `.claude/skills/` — repo-local Claude skills (read but do not require user
  invocation; skills triggered by `/skill-name` are listed at session start).

For Cursor and Codex parity, see `.cursor/rules/code-quality-gate.mdc` and
`.codex/agents/`. The validation flow is intentionally identical across all
three agents — keep it that way when updating one.

## Deeper guidance

Same per-topic docs as the other agents — start with these when working in a
specific surface:

- [Code quality & enforcement](docs/agents/code-quality.md)
- [Frontend](docs/agents/frontend.md)
- [Backend](docs/agents/backend.md)
- [Testing patterns](docs/agents/testing.md)
- [Domain model & AI pipeline](docs/agents/domain.md)
- [Feature inventory](docs/feature-inventory.md)
- [Resource ownership and sharing](docs/resource-ownership-sharing.md)
- [Pulse architecture](docs/pulse-architecture.md)
- [Goal Navigation](docs/goal-navigation.md)
- [Persona journey navigation](docs/persona-journey-navigation.md)
- [Personas, Audiences, and chats](docs/personas.md)
- [Dynamic website analysis](docs/dynamic-website-analysis.md)
- [Figma integration](docs/figma-integration.md)
- [Sentiment Maps](docs/sentiment-maps.md)
- [Entire session capture](docs/agents/entire.md)
- [Deployment & infra](docs/agents/deployment.md)
- [Development commands](docs/agents/dev.md)
- [Current product/platform map](docs/product-platform-guide.md)
- [External native Pulse intake](docs/external-pulse-intake-launch.md)
- [Report PDF export](docs/report-pdf-export.md)
- [Compare](docs/compare.md)
- [Documentation maintenance checklist](docs/agents/documentation-maintenance.md)

Before changing product visibility, sharing, report access, or resource lists,
read `docs/resource-ownership-sharing.md`. The current model is owner/private by
default inside an Auth0 tenant, with explicit same-org user or Team shares. Do
not infer org-wide visibility from `org_id`.

## Pulse shortcut and cross-repo rules

- Map and reuse the current `/pulse` service flow before changing
  create-and-launch or another shortcut endpoint. Do not patch the route with a
  second orchestration.
- `/pulse` is the current product flow. The launcher offers Single or Multiple
  Pages plus Compare; Set Path accepts URLs or PNG/JPEG/PDF uploads without
  mixing source types; Agent Path accepts one starting URL and uses Goal
  Navigation. The setup wizard proceeds through Assets, Goals, Personas, Tasks,
  then Findings; goal context files and Context Packs attach in the Goals step.
- Internal `legacy` names do not make a native Pulse imported.
- Explicit imported/read-only state and external-reference metadata are
  different concepts. A native Pulse may reference customer-api without using
  customer-api auth or data paths.
- Never use JSON `LIKE`/substring lookup on JSON columns; prefer typed
  idempotency columns or exact JSONB operators.
- customer-app payloads must compile against the current
  `@wevo/pulse-api-client` request type. Cross-repo endpoints require typed
  request/response, example fixture, contract tests, and version instructions.
- Goal Navigation PDFs iterate ordered `pageIds`/`assetIds` and load each
  page's findings with its page/asset id and `findings_run_id`.
- All Quant Compute tasks use the customer-api bridge, including native Journey
  and Goal Navigation scoring. They must not call Artemis directly or depend on
  `ARTEMIS_BASE_URL`.
- Preserve completed journey pages when a Urlbox/target 403 can be represented
  as a page-level blocked warning.
- Include request IDs and allocated session/findings/task IDs in cross-repo
  failure reports, without logging credentials or private payloads.

## Code Style

- Always strive for concise, simple solutions.
- If a problem
  can be solved in a simpler way, propose it.

## General preferences

- If asked to do too much work at once, stop and state that clearly.
- If computer use is helpful for completing or verifying work, shell out to gpt-5.5 with Codex for it

## Picking the right models for workflows and subagents

Rankings, higher = better. Cost reflects what I actually pay (OpenAI has really generous limits), not list price. Intelligence is how hard a problem you can hand the model unsupervised. Taste covers UI/UX, code quality, API design, and copy.

| model    | cost | intelligence | taste |
| -------- | ---- | ------------ | ----- |
| gpt-5.5  | 9    | 8            | 5     |
| sonnet-5 | 5    | 5            | 7     |
| opus-4.8 | 4    | 7            | 8     |
| fable-5  | 2    | 9            | 9     |

How to apply:

- These are defaults, not limits. You have standing permission to override them: if a cheaper model's output doesn't meet the bar, rerun or redo the work with a smarter model without asking. Judge the output, not the price tag. Escalating costs less than shipping mediocre work.
- Cost is a tie-breaker only; when axes conflict for anything that ships, intelligence > taste > cost.
- Bulk/mechanical work (clear-spec implementation, data analysis, migrations): gpt-5.5 — it's effectively free.
- Anything user-facing (UI, copy, API design) needs taste ≥ 7.
- Reviews of plans/implementations: fable-5 or opus-4.8, optionally gpt-5.5 as an extra independent perspective.
- Never use Haiku.
- Mechanics: gpt-5.5 is only reachable through the Codex CLI — `codex exec` / `codex review` (my `~/.codex/config.toml` defaults to gpt-5.5). Use the codex-implementation, codex-review, and codex-computer-use skills; for work they don't cover (investigation, data analysis), run `codex exec -s read-only` directly with a self-contained prompt.
- Claude models (sonnet-5, opus-4.8, fable-5) run via the Agent/Workflow model parameter.

Using gpt-5.5 inside workflows and subagents (the model parameter only takes Claude models, so use a wrapper):

- Spawn a thin Claude wrapper agent with `model: 'sonnet', effort: 'low'` whose prompt instructs it to write a self-contained Codex prompt, run `codex exec` via Bash, and return Codex’s output.
- The wrapper should not do the implementation itself. Its job is to delegate the actual work to Codex, collect the result, and report back clearly.
- For implementation work, have the wrapper run `codex exec` with permission to edit files.
- For investigations, analysis, or safety checks, have the wrapper run `codex exec -s read-only` so it can inspect the repo without changing anything.
- For reviews, have the wrapper run `codex review` with the relevant diff, files, or plan.
- Keep the Codex prompt self-contained. Include the task, repo context, relevant files, constraints, acceptance criteria, and whether Codex is allowed to edit files.
- The wrapper’s final response should include what Codex changed or found, any commands it ran, test results, risks, and remaining follow-ups.

Using gpt-5.5 inside workflows and subagents (the model parameter only takes Claude models, so use a wrapper):

- Spawn a thin Claude wrapper agent with `model: 'sonnet', effort: 'low'` whose prompt instructs it to write a self-contained codex prompt, run `codex exec` via Bash, and return the report (use 'schema' on the wrapper to get structured output back).
- Always label these agents with a 'gpt-5.5:' prefix, e.g. '{label: 'gpt-5.5: review-auth'}' - the workflow UI shows the wrapper's Claude model, so the label is the only indication the real worker is gpt-5.5.
- Codex runs can exceed Bash's 10-minute timeout: pass an explicit timeout, or run in the background and poll for the report file.
- Parallel gpt-5.5 implementation agents must use 'isolation: 'worktree'' so codex edits don't collide in the shared checkout.
- Workflow token budgets only count Claude tokens; codex work is free and invisible to
  'budget.spent()'.

# Code Quality Gate (Claude Code)

This is the Claude Code counterpart of [.cursor/rules/code-quality-gate.mdc](../../.cursor/rules/code-quality-gate.mdc).
Claude Code has no automatic `alwaysApply` mechanism for repo-local rules —
`CLAUDE.md` at the repo root is what is loaded automatically. This file exists
so the policy lives in `.claude/rules/` alongside its Cursor / Codex peers and
so future sessions can grep for it the same way they grep `.cursor/rules/`.

**Every iteration must pass targeted `make code-quality`; every completed chunk must pass `make finish-work`. No exceptions.**

## Workflow

1. During normal iteration, run `make code-quality` from the repo root.
2. In shared worktrees, prefer explicit changed-file traces via
   `CODE_QUALITY_CHANGED_FILES`, `CODE_QUALITY_CHANGED_FILES_FILE`, or
   repeated `--changed-file` arguments so one agent does not inherit another
   agent's dirty paths. If your work is already committed, use the
   `CODE_QUALITY_BASE` / `CODE_QUALITY_HEAD` / `CODE_QUALITY_COMPARISON=range`
   trio instead.
3. If **any** targeted step fails, fix the failure and re-run until it passes.
4. When the chunk is complete, run `make finish-work` with `PATCH_CHANGELOG_*`
   metadata (see [CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md) for the env var contract). It
   runs the targeted gate over the whole branch; CI owns the full suite.
   `FINISH_WORK_SCOPE=full` also runs it locally, behind one machine-wide slot
   shared by every worktree. Wait for the slot rather than starting competing
   runs.
5. Only after a clean `make finish-work` run may you report the task as
   complete.

## Hard rules

- **Do not** substitute ad-hoc `ruff check` / `mypy` / `pytest` calls for
  `make code-quality`. The gate also runs format/syntax/contract checks,
  enforces produced-artifact freshness, and stages pending finish-work receipts
  when `PATCH_CHANGELOG_*` is set; bare tool calls skip all of that.
- **Do not** bypass with `git commit --no-verify`. The pre-commit hook exists
  for the same reason as the gate.
- **Do not** silence errors with `any`, `@ts-ignore`, `type: ignore`,
  `eslint-disable`, or `noqa` unless strictly unavoidable and documented with
  a comment explaining why.
- **Do not** delete tests to make the gate pass. Tests may only be deleted
  when the feature they cover is removed in the same change.

## Common Claude-specific pitfalls

- macOS system `python3` is 3.9 and breaks `scripts/run_code_quality.py` at
  import time (`from datetime import UTC` is 3.11+). Prefix the command with
  `PATH="$(pwd)/backend/.venv/bin:$PATH"` when running the gate from the repo
  root.
- Claude Code can run from a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/<name>/`. Edit /
  Write tools accept absolute paths and will write to whatever path you give
  them — including the **main repo's working tree** if the path lives there.
  Confirm the working tree's branch with `git -C <path> rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`
  before staging / running the gate.
- The gate reads `PATCH_CHANGELOG_*` from the environment when it runs. If you
  set those vars and run `make code-quality`, the gate stages a pending
  finish-work receipt that a later `make finish-work` will drain. Setting
  them upfront is the recommended flow for a known-complete chunk.
- A successful finish creates a unique immutable fragment under
  `changesets/patch/`. `PATCH_CHANGELOG.md` is frozen legacy history.

## See also

- [CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md) — repo-root Claude entrypoint
- [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) — canonical agent guide (universal)
- [docs/agents/code-quality.md](../../docs/agents/code-quality.md) — deeper
  reference on what each step checks and how to fix failures
- [.cursor/rules/code-quality-gate.mdc](../../.cursor/rules/code-quality-gate.mdc) —
  Cursor counterpart (kept in sync with this file)

# Claude Code — wevo-pulse agent guide

This is the Claude-specific entrypoint. The canonical agent guide is
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md); the items below either mirror policy that all agents
share or document things that only apply to Claude Code.

> If something is in `AGENTS.md` and not here, the AGENTS.md version wins.

## Validation flow (mandatory)

The validation gates are identical for Claude, Cursor, and Codex. Follow them:

1. **During normal iteration**, run `make code-quality` from the repo root. It
   validates changed worktree files only.
   - If anything fails, **fix the failure** and re-run until it passes. Do not
     skip a step with `# type: ignore`, `eslint-disable`, `noqa`, or by deleting
     the failing test (see "Test deletion policy" below).
   - **Do not substitute** ad-hoc `ruff check` / `mypy` / `pytest` calls for
     `make code-quality`. The gate also runs format/syntax/contract checks and
     records pending finish-work receipts when `PATCH_CHANGELOG_*` is set; bare
     tool calls skip all of that.
2. **When a chunk is complete**, run `make finish-work` with
   `PATCH_CHANGELOG_*` metadata. It runs the targeted gate over the whole
   branch (everything since the `origin/main` merge base, plus dirty and
   untracked files) and records the chunk's intent as an immutable, uniquely
   named fragment under `changesets/patch/YYYY-MM/`. CI runs the full suite on
   the PR and the merge-queue commit, and nothing merges or releases without
   it. Set `FINISH_WORK_SCOPE=full` to also run the full suite locally.
   - Local full suites (`make code-quality-full`, `FINISH_WORK_SCOPE=full`)
     take one machine-wide slot shared by every worktree. A waiting run prints
     which worktree holds it. Do not work around the wait by lowering worker
     counts or starting another run. Backend failures get one serial retry,
     and anything that passes only on retry is listed as a load flake.
3. **Only after a clean `make finish-work` run** may you report the chunk as
   complete.

### Scoping the gate to your work in a shared / dirty worktree

When other agents (or you, from a prior session) have unrelated work in the
worktree, the targeted gate's default `worktree-vs-HEAD` detection sweeps in
their files too. Use one of the supported overrides instead:

```bash
# Option A — explicit file list (best when you already know what you touched)
make code-quality \
  CODE_QUALITY_CHANGED_FILES="$(git diff --name-only HEAD -- backend/path/to/your/file.py | jq -R . | jq -s .)"

# Option B — git diff range (best when your work is already committed)
CODE_QUALITY_BASE=HEAD^ \
CODE_QUALITY_HEAD=HEAD \
CODE_QUALITY_COMPARISON=range \
make code-quality

# Option C — pass --changed-file directly to the underlying script (bypasses make)
backend/.venv/bin/python scripts/run_code_quality.py \
  --changed-file backend/path/to/your/file.py \
  --changed-file backend/tests/test_your_file.py
```

`make finish-work` accepts `FINISH_WORK_CHANGED_FILES`,
`FINISH_WORK_CHANGED_FILES_FILE`, and repeated `--changed-file` flags for the
same purpose.

If `PATCH_CHANGELOG_*` is already set during a successful
`make code-quality`, the repo stages a pending finish-work receipt. A later
successful `make finish-work` drains those receipts. Setting the
`PATCH_CHANGELOG_*` env vars before `make code-quality` is the recommended
flow when you know up-front you are about to finish a chunk.

`PATCH_CHANGELOG.md` is frozen legacy history. Use
`make patch-changelog-render` for a combined view. On an older open branch that
still added entries to the legacy file, run `make patch-changelog-migrate`
before syncing with `main`.

Required when running `make finish-work`:

- `PATCH_CHANGELOG_SUMMARY` — one-line summary of the chunk
- `PATCH_CHANGELOG_INTENT` — _why_ this change was made, in product/system terms
- `PATCH_CHANGELOG_OUTCOME` — what the change accomplishes after merge

Optional:

- `PATCH_CHANGELOG_SCOPE` — directories / surfaces touched (e.g. `backend, docs`)
- `PATCH_CHANGELOG_WHY`, `PATCH_CHANGELOG_ISSUE`, `PATCH_CHANGELOG_NOTES`, `PATCH_CHANGELOG_AUTHOR`
- `SEMVER_CHANGESET_FILE` — path to a `changesets/semver/*.yaml` if governed
  surfaces (OpenAPI, generated clients, Auth0 / infra contracts) changed

Example:

```bash
PATCH_CHANGELOG_SUMMARY="Add Responses API path for o-series models" \
PATCH_CHANGELOG_INTENT="o3-pro was silently downgrading to gpt-4o on chat completions, breaking artemis parity." \
PATCH_CHANGELOG_OUTCOME="Legacy exact-mode findings route every o-series step through the Responses API." \
PATCH_CHANGELOG_SCOPE="backend/app/services/ai, backend/app/services/legacy" \
make finish-work
```

The bare `python3` on macOS is the system Python 3.9, which is missing
`datetime.UTC` and breaks `scripts/run_code_quality.py` at import time. Always
put the backend uv venv on `PATH` first when running the gate:

```bash
PATH="$(pwd)/backend/.venv/bin:$PATH" make code-quality
```

Inside the `backend/` directory the venv is already on `PATH` via `uv run`, so
this only matters at the repo root.

### Fixing failures

- **Format**: run `make format`, re-run `make code-quality`.
- **Lint**: fix the flagged code. Do not suppress with `eslint-disable` /
  `noqa` unless documented and unavoidable.
- **Types**: fix the types. No `any`, `@ts-ignore`, or `type: ignore` unless

```bash

git -C /Users/.../wevo-pulse/.claude/worktrees/<name> rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD  # worktree branch
```

## Pulse shortcut and cross-repo rules

- Map and reuse the current `/pulse` service flow before changing
  create-and-launch or another shortcut endpoint. Do not patch the route with a
  second orchestration.
- `/pulse` is the current product flow. The launcher offers Single or Multiple
  Pages plus Compare; Set Path accepts URLs or PNG/JPEG/PDF uploads without
  mixing source types; Agent Path accepts one starting URL and uses Goal
  Navigation. The setup wizard proceeds through Assets, Goals, Personas, Tasks,
  then Findings; goal context files and Context Packs attach in the Goals step.
- Internal `legacy` names do not make a native Pulse imported.
- Explicit imported/read-only state and external-reference metadata are
  different concepts. A native Pulse may reference customer-api without using
  customer-api auth or data paths.
- Never use JSON `LIKE`/substring lookup on JSON columns; prefer typed
  idempotency columns or exact JSONB operators.
- customer-app payloads must compile against the current
  `@wevo/pulse-api-client` request type. Cross-repo endpoints require typed
  request/response, example fixture, contract tests, and version instructions.
- Goal Navigation PDFs iterate ordered `pageIds`/`assetIds` and load each
  page's findings with its page/asset id and `findings_run_id`.
- All Quant Compute tasks use the customer-api bridge, including native Journey
  and Goal Navigation scoring. They must not call Artemis directly or depend on
  `ARTEMIS_BASE_URL`.
- Preserve completed journey pages when a Urlbox/target 403 can be represented
  as a page-level blocked warning.
- Include request IDs and allocated session/findings/task IDs in cross-repo
  failure reports, without logging credentials or private payloads.

- Always strive for concise, simple solutions.

## Picking the right models for workflows and subagents

Rankings, higher = better. Cost reflects what I actually pay (OpenAI has really generous limits), not list price. Intelligence is how hard a problem you can hand the model unsupervised. Taste covers UI/UX, code quality, API design, and copy.

| model    | cost | intelligence | taste |
| -------- | ---- | ------------ | ----- |
| gpt-5.5  | 9    | 8            | 5     |
| sonnet-5 | 5    | 5            | 7     |
| opus-4.8 | 4    | 7            | 8     |
| fable-5  | 2    | 9            | 9     |

How to apply:

- These are defaults, not limits. You have standing permission to override them: if a cheaper model's output doesn't meet the bar, rerun or redo the work with a smarter model without asking. Judge the output, not the price tag. Escalating costs less than shipping mediocre work.
- Cost is a tie-breaker only; when axes conflict for anything that ships, intelligence > taste > cost.
- Bulk/mechanical work (clear-spec implementation, data analysis, migrations): gpt-5.5 — it's effectively free.
- Anything user-facing (UI, copy, API design) needs taste ≥ 7.
- Reviews of plans/implementations: fable-5 or opus-4.8, optionally gpt-5.5 as an extra independent perspective.
- Never use Haiku.

Use the codex-implementation, codex-review, and codex-computer-use skills; for work they don't cover (investigation, data analysis), run `codex exec -s read-only` directly with a self-contained prompt.
- Claude models (sonnet-5, opus-4.8, fable-5) run via the Agent/Workflow model parameter.

Using gpt-5.5 inside workflows and subagents (the model parameter only takes Claude models, so use a wrapper):

- Spawn a thin Claude wrapper agent with `model: 'sonnet', effort: 'low'` whose prompt instructs it to write a self-contained Codex prompt, run `codex exec` via Bash, and return Codex’s output.
- The wrapper should not do the implementation itself. Its job is to delegate the actual work to Codex, collect the result, and report back clearly.
- For implementation work, have the wrapper run `codex exec` with permission to edit files.
- For investigations, analysis, or safety checks, have the wrapper run `codex exec -s read-only` so it can inspect the repo without changing anything.
- For reviews, have the wrapper run `codex review` with the relevant diff, files, or plan.
- Keep the Codex prompt self-contained. Include the task, repo context, relevant files, constraints, acceptance criteria, and whether Codex is allowed to edit files.
- The wrapper’s final response should include what Codex changed or found, any commands it ran, test results, risks, and remaining follow-ups.

# Code Quality Gate (Claude Code)

This is the Claude Code counterpart of [.cursor/rules/code-quality-gate.mdc](../../.cursor/rules/code-quality-gate.mdc).
Claude Code has no automatic `alwaysApply` mechanism for repo-local rules —
`CLAUDE.md` at the repo root is what is loaded automatically. This file exists
so the policy lives in `.claude/rules/` alongside its Cursor / Codex peers and
so future sessions can grep for it the same way they grep `.cursor/rules/`.

**Every iteration must pass targeted `make code-quality`; every completed chunk must pass `make finish-work`. No exceptions.**

## Workflow

1. During normal iteration, run `make code-quality` from the repo root.
2. In shared worktrees, prefer explicit changed-file traces via
   `CODE_QUALITY_CHANGED_FILES`, `CODE_QUALITY_CHANGED_FILES_FILE`, or
   repeated `--changed-file` arguments so one agent does not inherit another
   agent's dirty paths. If your work is already committed, use the
   `CODE_QUALITY_BASE` / `CODE_QUALITY_HEAD` / `CODE_QUALITY_COMPARISON=range`
   trio instead.
3. If **any** targeted step fails, fix the failure and re-run until it passes.
4. When the chunk is complete, run `make finish-work` with `PATCH_CHANGELOG_*`
   metadata (see [CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md) for the env var contract). It
   runs the targeted gate over the whole branch; CI owns the full suite.
   `FINISH_WORK_SCOPE=full` also runs it locally, behind one machine-wide slot
   shared by every worktree. Wait for the slot rather than starting competing
   runs.
5. Only after a clean `make finish-work` run may you report the task as
   complete.

## Hard rules

- **Do not** substitute ad-hoc `ruff check` / `mypy` / `pytest` calls for
  `make code-quality`. The gate also runs format/syntax/contract checks,
  enforces produced-artifact freshness, and stages pending finish-work receipts
  when `PATCH_CHANGELOG_*` is set; bare tool calls skip all of that.
- **Do not** bypass with `git commit --no-verify`. The pre-commit hook exists
  for the same reason as the gate.
- **Do not** silence errors with `any`, `@ts-ignore`, `type: ignore`,
  `eslint-disable`, or `noqa` unless strictly unavoidable and documented with
  a comment explaining why.
- **Do not** delete tests to make the gate pass. Tests may only be deleted
  when the feature they cover is removed in the same change.

## Common Claude-specific pitfalls

- macOS system `python3` is 3.9 and breaks `scripts/run_code_quality.py` at
  import time (`from datetime import UTC` is 3.11+). Prefix the command with
  `PATH="$(pwd)/backend/.venv/bin:$PATH"` when running the gate from the repo
  root.
- Claude Code can run from a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/<name>/`. Edit /
  Write tools accept absolute paths and will write to whatever path you give
  them — including the **main repo's working tree** if the path lives there.
  Confirm the working tree's branch with `git -C <path> rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`
  before staging / running the gate.
- The gate reads `PATCH_CHANGELOG_*` from the environment when it runs. If you
  set those vars and run `make code-quality`, the gate stages a pending
  finish-work receipt that a later `make finish-work` will drain. Setting
  them upfront is the recommended flow for a known-complete chunk.
- A successful finish creates a unique immutable fragment under
  `changesets/patch/`. `PATCH_CHANGELOG.md` is frozen legacy history.

"""Credential-free tests for the company Pulse report merge and reconciliation logic."""

import importlib.util
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

MODULE_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "report_company_pulses.py"
SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("report_company_pulses", MODULE_PATH)
assert SPEC and SPEC.loader
module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)
SPEC.loader.exec_module(module)

LEGACY_ID = "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111"
NATIVE_ID = "22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222"
NAV_ID = "33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333"
TASK_ID = "44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444444"


def _legacy(**overrides):
    row = {
        "pulse_id": LEGACY_ID,
        "session_type": "experience",
        "name": "Legacy pulse",
        "owner_email": "a@accenture.com",
        "owner_user_id": "7",
        "team_id": "138",
        "team_name": "Accenture Interactive",
        "created_at": "2026-08-05T10:00:00Z",
        "deleted_at": None,
        "completed_at": "2026-08-05T11:00:00Z",
        "growthos_project_id": "proj-1",
        "receipt_events": 0,
        "receipt_delivered": 0,
        "receipt_failed": 0,
        "last_delivered_at": None,
        "delivered_cost": None,
    }
    row.update(overrides)
    return row


def _native(**overrides):
    row = {
        "pulse_id": NATIVE_ID,
        "source_system": "native",
        "import_status": "native",
        "source_session_id": None,
        "session_type": "experience",
        "state": "findings_ready",
        "name": "Native pulse",
        "owner_sub": "samlp|org-x-sso-connection|b@accenture.com",
        "dir_email": None,
        "dir_name_id": None,
        "dir_resolved_email": None,
        "created_at": "2026-10-20 10:00:00+00:00",
        "updated_at": "2026-10-20 12:00:00+00:00",
        "source_created_at": None,
        "deleted_at": None,
        "growthos_project_id": "proj-2",
        "journey_mode": None,
        "credit_team_id": None,
        "findings_completed_at": "2026-10-20 11:00:00+00:00",
    }
    row.update(overrides)
    return row


def _inputs(**overrides):
    values = {
        "company": {
            "company_id": "136",
            "org_id": "org_x",
            "outbox_first_event_at": "2026-09-15T00:00:00Z",
            "_sows": [
                {"sow_id": "s", "created_at": "2026-10-14T00:00:00Z", "team_ids": "138", "deleted_at": None}
            ],
        },
        "teams": [{"team_id": "138", "team_name": "Accenture Interactive"}, {"team_id": "18065", "team_name": ""}],
        "users": [{"email": "b@accenture.com", "user_id": "9", "team_ids": "138"}],
        "legacy": [_legacy()],
        "pulse_sessions": [
            _native(),
            # Mirror of the legacy Pulse; must not produce a second row.
            _native(
                pulse_id=LEGACY_ID,
                source_system="customer_api",
                import_status="detail_synced",
                source_session_id=LEGACY_ID,
            ),
        ],
        "receipts": [],
        "ledger": [],
        "task_map": [],
    }
    values.update(overrides)
    return module.ReportInputs(**values)


def _by_id(rows):
    return {r["pulse_id"]: r for r in rows}


class ReportCompanyPulsesTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_legacy_mirror_is_deduplicated_and_annotated(self):
        rows, _ = module.build_rows(_inputs())
        self.assertEqual(len(rows), 2)
        legacy = _by_id(rows)[LEGACY_ID]
        self.assertEqual(legacy["source"], "legacy")
        self.assertEqual(legacy["pulse_db_mirror"], "detail_synced")
        # Completed before the outbox existed, so no durable receipt can exist.
        self.assertEqual(legacy["growthos_delivery_status"], "unrecorded_pre_outbox")

    def test_native_owner_email_and_team_fall_back_to_sub_and_membership(self):
        native = _by_id(module.build_rows(_inputs())[0])[NATIVE_ID]
        self.assertEqual(native["owner_email"], "b@accenture.com")
        self.assertEqual(native["owner_user_id"], "9")
        self.assertEqual(native["team_id"], "138")
        self.assertEqual(native["growthos_delivery_status"], "missing")

    def test_receipts_flag_duplicates_failures_and_5xx_retries(self):
        receipts = [
            {"pulse_id": NATIVE_ID, "final_status": "succeeded", "delivered_at": "2026-10-20T11:00:00Z",
             "cost": "1", "http_5xx": 1},
            {"pulse_id": NATIVE_ID, "final_status": "succeeded", "delivered_at": "2026-10-20T11:30:00Z",
             "cost": "1", "http_5xx": 0},
        ]
        native = _by_id(module.build_rows(_inputs(receipts=receipts))[0])[NATIVE_ID]

"""Credential-free tests for the company Pulse report merge and reconciliation logic."""

import importlib.util
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

MODULE_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "report_company_pulses.py"
SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("report_company_pulses", MODULE_PATH)
assert SPEC and SPEC.loader
module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)
SPEC.loader.exec_module(module)

LEGACY_ID = "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111"
NATIVE_ID = "22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222"
NAV_ID = "33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333"
TASK_ID = "44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444444"


def _legacy(**overrides):
    row = {
        "pulse_id": LEGACY_ID,
        "session_type": "experience",
        "name": "Legacy pulse",
        "owner_email": "a@accenture.com",
        "owner_user_id": "7",
        "team_id": "138",
        "team_name": "Accenture Interactive",
        "created_at": "2026-08-05T10:00:00Z",
        "deleted_at": None,
        "completed_at": "2026-08-05T11:00:00Z",
        "growthos_project_id": "proj-1",
        "receipt_events": 0,
        "receipt_delivered": 0,
        "receipt_failed": 0,
        "last_delivered_at": None,
        "delivered_cost": None,
    }
    row.update(overrides)
    return row


def _native(**overrides):
    row = {
        "pulse_id": NATIVE_ID,
        "source_system": "native",
        "import_status": "native",
        "source_session_id": None,
        "session_type": "experience",
        "state": "findings_ready",
        "name": "Native pulse",
        "owner_sub": "samlp|org-x-sso-connection|b@accenture.com",
        "dir_email": None,
        "dir_name_id": None,
        "dir_resolved_email": None,
        "created_at": "2026-10-20 10:00:00+00:00",
        "updated_at": "2026-10-20 12:00:00+00:00",
        "source_created_at": None,
        "deleted_at": None,
        "growthos_project_id": "proj-2",
        "journey_mode": None,
        "credit_team_id": None,
        "findings_completed_at": "2026-10-20 11:00:00+00:00",
    }
    row.update(overrides)
    return row


def _inputs(**overrides):
    values = {
        "company": {
            "company_id": "136",
            "org_id": "org_x",
            "outbox_first_event_at": "2026-09-15T00:00:00Z",
            "_sows": [
                {"sow_id": "s", "created_at": "2026-10-14T00:00:00Z", "team_ids": "138", "deleted_at": None}
            ],
        },
        "teams": [{"team_id": "138", "team_name": "Accenture Interactive"}, {"team_id": "18065", "team_name": ""}],
        "users": [{"email": "b@accenture.com", "user_id": "9", "team_ids": "138"}],
        "legacy": [_legacy()],
        "pulse_sessions": [
            _native(),
            # Mirror of the legacy Pulse; must not produce a second row.
            _native(
                pulse_id=LEGACY_ID,
                source_system="customer_api",
                import_status="detail_synced",
                source_session_id=LEGACY_ID,
            ),
        ],
        "receipts": [],
        "ledger": [],
        "task_map": [],
    }
    values.update(overrides)
    return module.ReportInputs(**values)


def _by_id(rows):
    return {r["pulse_id"]: r for r in rows}


class ReportCompanyPulsesTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_legacy_mirror_is_deduplicated_and_annotated(self):
        rows, _ = module.build_rows(_inputs())
        self.assertEqual(len(rows), 2)
        legacy = _by_id(rows)[LEGACY_ID]
        self.assertEqual(legacy["source"], "legacy")
        self.assertEqual(legacy["pulse_db_mirror"], "detail_synced")
        # Completed before the outbox existed, so no durable receipt can exist.
        self.assertEqual(legacy["growthos_delivery_status"], "unrecorded_pre_outbox")

    def test_native_owner_email_and_team_fall_back_to_sub_and_membership(self):
        native = _by_id(module.build_rows(_inputs())[0])[NATIVE_ID]
        self.assertEqual(native["owner_email"], "b@accenture.com")
        self.assertEqual(native["owner_user_id"], "9")
        self.assertEqual(native["team_id"], "138")
        self.assertEqual(native["growthos_delivery_status"], "missing")

    def test_receipts_flag_duplicates_failures_and_5xx_retries(self):
        receipts = [
            {"pulse_id": NATIVE_ID, "final_status": "succeeded", "delivered_at": "2026-10-20T11:00:00Z",
             "cost": "1", "http_5xx": 1},
            {"pulse_id": NATIVE_ID, "final_status": "succeeded", "delivered_at": "2026-10-20T11:30:00Z",
             "cost": "1", "http_5xx": 0},
        ]
        native = _by_id(module.build_rows(_inputs(receipts=receipts))[0])[NATIVE_ID]
        self.assertEqual(native["growthos_delivery_status"], "delivered_multiple")
        self.assertEqual(native["growthos_cost"], "2")
        self.assertTrue(native["growthos_retry_500"])

        failed = [{"pulse_id": NATIVE_ID, "final_status": "failed", "error_summary": "required_userId_missing"}]
        native = _by_id(module.build_rows(_inputs(receipts=failed))[0])[NATIVE_ID]
        self.assertEqual(native["growthos_delivery_status"], "failed:required_userId_missing")

    def test_ledger_entries_map_through_findings_task(self):
        ledger = [
            {"ledger_entry_id": "h", "type": "usage_hold", "event_type": "pulse", "amount": "1.0000",
             "linked_artifact_id": TASK_ID, "team_id": "138"},
            {"ledger_entry_id": "r", "type": "hold_release", "event_type": "pulse", "amount": "-1.0000",
             "linked_artifact_id": TASK_ID, "team_id": "138"},
            {"ledger_entry_id": "c", "type": "usage_commit", "event_type": "pulse", "amount": "1.0000",
             "linked_artifact_id": TASK_ID, "team_id": "138"},
            {"ledger_entry_id": "x", "type": "usage_commit", "event_type": "pulse", "amount": "3.0000",
             "linked_artifact_id": "unknown-task", "team_id": "138"},
        ]
        task_map = [{"task_id": TASK_ID, "pulse_id": NATIVE_ID, "team_id": "138"}]
        rows, extra = module.build_rows(_inputs(ledger=ledger, task_map=task_map))
        native = _by_id(rows)[NATIVE_ID]
        self.assertEqual(native["ledger_entry_ids"], "c")
        self.assertEqual(native["ledger_amount_committed"], "1")
        self.assertEqual(native["ledger_amount_open_hold"], "")
        self.assertEqual(native["credit_basis"], "ledger")
        self.assertEqual([e["ledger_entry_id"] for e in extra["unmatched_ledger"]], ["x"])

    def test_ai_nav_is_classified_and_kept_out_of_the_draft_import(self):
        nav = _native(pulse_id=NAV_ID, journey_mode="navigation_journey")
        inputs = _inputs(pulse_sessions=[_native(), nav])
        rows, _ = module.build_rows(inputs)
        self.assertEqual(_by_id(rows)[NAV_ID]["pulse_kind"], "ai_nav")
        drafts = module.draft_import_rows(rows, {"138"})
        self.assertEqual(sorted(d["artifactId"] for d in drafts), sorted([LEGACY_ID, NATIVE_ID]))
        self.assertTrue(all(d["poolType"] == "token" and d["amount"] == "1" for d in drafts))

    def test_draft_uses_the_single_sow_team_and_estimated_completion(self):
        users = [{"email": "b@accenture.com", "user_id": "9", "team_ids": "138;18065"}]
        session = _native(findings_completed_at=None)
        rows, _ = module.build_rows(_inputs(users=users, legacy=[], pulse_sessions=[session]))
        native = _by_id(rows)[NATIVE_ID]
        self.assertEqual(native["team_id"], "138;18065")
        self.assertEqual(native["completed_at"], "2026-10-20T12:00:00Z")
        drafts = module.draft_import_rows(rows, {"138"})
        self.assertEqual([(d["teamId"], d["occurredAt"]) for d in drafts], [("138", "2026-10-20T12:00:00Z")])
        self.assertEqual(module.draft_import_rows(rows, {"999"}), [])

    def test_summary_reconciles_ledger_gaps_and_undelivered_growthos(self):
        inputs = _inputs()
        rows, extra = module.build_rows(inputs)
        summary = module.summarize(rows, inputs, extra)
        self.assertEqual(summary["totals"]["pulses"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(summary["native_completed_since_ledger_start_without_commit"], [NATIVE_ID])
        self.assertEqual(summary["growthos_undelivered"], [NATIVE_ID])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

Base directory for this skill: /Users/ryanbigelow/.claude-easycliproxy/skills/sol-loop

# sol-loop

This is a workflow for making your code changes more correct before (or
sometimes after) filing a pull request. tl;dr - use OpenAI's GPT Sol to review
your code in a loop.

Make the most minimal possible changes to appease the Sol reviewers. Be careful
of scope creep and don't be scared to push back.

## Budget

- Default: 3 rounds total. Round 1 is full. Later rounds check only
  changed code and open findings.
- Extend to 5 only for security, permissions, auth, data loss, or
  state/concurrency, while a blocker or should stays open with evidence. Or when
  the user asks.
- Stop early if a round returns only nits. Declined nits and comment,
  doc, or format-only fixes need no new round.
- One reviewer only. Sol must not start subagents or reviewers.
- Keep a ledger: id, severity, outcome, usage if returned. Never guess it.

## 1. Scope

Run `git status --short`. Do not stash, discard, or include unrelated
changes. Limit review to the change paths if they separate cleanly.
Otherwise stop and ask.

Find the base after `git fetch origin`:

- PR: `gh pr view <n> --json baseRefName,headRefOid`. Check out the branch
  only if clean. Confirm `HEAD` is the PR head, or ahead only by this
  change. Base: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<baseRefName>`.
- Local: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<default-branch>`. No remote: a base
  the user names, or `HEAD` for uncommitted changes only.

The change is base to working tree in those paths, with untracked files.
Use one diff command all rounds. State intent and out-of-scope in 1-2
sentences. Run covering checks. Do not send code this change breaks. Note
missing or pre-failing checks in the brief.

## 2. Start Sol

In T3, call `orchestrator_capabilities`. Pick the latest Sol unless the user
named a version. Do not hardcode an ID. Record provider, model, and effort
only if exposed. Use `delegate_task` every round (`role: "review"`,
`mode: "async"`). Save `taskId`. New `clientRequestId` per round.
`childThreadId` is storage, not the next target. Do not use
`t3_thread_send`, `create_threads`, or `t3_thread_launch` for review.

If T3 tools are not listed, try one direct capability call. Outside T3, use
a native Sol subagent and keep its ID. In Claude Code, use a custom subagent
only if it is set up to run Sol. If no route runs Sol, report the blocker. Do
not substitute a model.

Do not edit scoped files while review runs. Wait for the notice. Do not
poll or start a second reviewer. Timeout, error, or no reply is not
approval. On failure, cancel, verify stop, restart with the ledger.

Round 1 brief (T3 children get no history):

```
Review only. Do not edit, commit, push, comment on PRs, or start subagents.
Repo: <abs path> Base: <sha> Intent: <intent> Out of scope: <scope> Checks: <results>
See: git diff <base> [-- <paths>]; git status --short (read untracked).
Read surrounding code. Find bugs, broken callers, mismatch with intent.
Skip style unless it hides a bug. Hold to the smallest change. Flag code,
tests, or guards the intent does not need. Other paths, rare cases, small
perf, extra compat: nits.
blocker = intended case wrong. should = real bug callers will hit, in intent. nit = rest.
Reply:
VERDICT: APPROVE or CHANGES
S1 [blocker|should|nit] <file>:<line> <claim>. Fix: <suggestion> (stable ids)
```

## 3. Answer findings

Check each finding and severity yourself. Another path, rare case, or
small cost is a nit, whatever label it came with.

- Agree: smallest fix. Prefer delete or narrow over new lock, cache,
  helper, or option. Fix the case that happened. Add one focused test
  that fails without the fix, if intent needs it.
- Disagree: say why, with evidence (file:line, test, output).
- Out of scope or nit: decline in one line. List as follow-up.

Update the ledger. Re-run checks and `git diff --shortstat <base>`. If
review grew the diff, cut first. Do not agree just to end the loop.

## 4. Next round

Start one only if budget remains and a blocker or should is open, behavior code
changed, or approval does not cover the current behavior diff. Use a fresh
`delegate_task` in T3, or follow up the saved native ID. Send the round 1 brief,
the ledger (`fixed:` / `disagree:` / `declined:` + evidence), the same base
diff, and the change since last round. Tell Sol: open ids and changed code only.
Mark each old id `resolved` or `still open: <reason>`.

## 5. Stop and ship

Agreed: APPROVE on the current behavior diff, no blocker or should open,
no concern of your own. Stuck: an item stays disputed after two replies,
or budget ends. Show both sides in 2-3 lines each. The user decides.
Budget end is not approval.

Do not push during the loop. Push after agreement only if the user asked
to push, ship, or update the PR. If you push to a PR, add above the model
blurb:

`Reviewed with sol-loop: <N> rounds with <model>. Sol verdict: approved`.

Add `on <effort>` only if verified.

Report: rounds, model, what Sol changed, diff size before/after, fixed and
declined findings with reasons, usage if exposed (else say not), pushed or not.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.
